# Base R Plots
![](/images/palette.png){style="width:200px; background: white; border-radius:5px; border: 5px white solid" fig-align="center"}

R is great for creating plots.
There are many great packages for creating plots such as [`ggplot2`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/).
however,  in this part I will show you how to create some plot types with base R.

## Setup

For setup:

1. Create a directory called "plots"
2. Set the newly created "plots" directory as your working directory
3. Create a new script within "plots" called "5-Plots.R" to use for this part

## Contents

This part's contents are described below.

### Plots
![](/images/histogram.png){style="width:150px; background: white; border-radius:5px; border: 5px white solid" fig-align="center"}

This part covers the creation and customisation of four different types of plots:

- [Histograms](/plots/histogram.qmd)
- [Line graphs](/plots/line.qmd)
- [Scatter plots](/plots/scatter.qmd)
- [Boxplots](/plots/boxplot.qmd)

### Misc

Between the plot sections are other topics. These are:

- [Previous plots](/plots/prev_plot.qmd): How to view previous plots you created in RStudio
- [Factors](/plots/factors.qmd): Factors are a class that contains levels
  - This section explains how they work and why they are useful
- [Save to png](/plots/png.qmd): Saving plots to png files

### Exercise
![](/images/penguin.png){style="width:150px; background:white; border-radius:5px" fig-align="center"}


At the end of this part are [four exercises](/plots/exercises.qmd), one for each plot type you have learnt through this part.
In each exercises you are tasked to create the displayed plots using a dataset of penguin populations.
